🌍 Tehran, Tashkent agree to expand long-term agricultural cooperation: Uzbekistan

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Uzbekistan and Iran have agreed to expand long-term cooperation in agriculture, pursue joint projects and strengthen ties between economic and business representatives, Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources announced.

According to Caspian Post, the ministry said representatives of the two countries met in Tashkent to discuss upgrading agricultural cooperation, developing existing relations and identifying priority areas for future collaboration.
​
Iranian Agriculture Minister Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh and his Uzbek counterpart, Ibrokhim Abdurakhmonov, emphasized the need to prepare a long-term cooperation program, implement mutually beneficial projects and expand links between private-sector and commercial representatives, the statement said.
​
Abdurakhmonov highlighted the importance of cooperation with Iranian companies, saying Tashkent was ready, within its authority, to support Iranian firms and the implementation of their new projects in Uzbekistan.
​
He also stressed the importance of regular and transparent dialogue among business representatives from the two countries.
​
Nouri Ghezeljeh said the Agricultural Business Forum between Iran and Uzbekistan provides an important platform for exchanging experience, presenting initiatives and expanding practical cooperation.
​
At the end of the meeting, the agriculture ministries of Iran and Uzbekistan signed a cooperation protocol. The two sides also signed several agreements covering various areas.
​
The agreements will provide a framework for developing agricultural ties, supporting joint projects and strengthening direct links between companies and government institutions in Iran and Uzbekistan.
